language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hello! I’m Thor, the god of thunder. I come from the world of Asgard. I have the power to control thunder and lightning. A thunderbolt strikes earth, when I fling down my hammer. Did you know that when lightning strikes, energy is released?
My powers and electricity have something in common. That's why I want to talk to you about electric circuits and how they relate to my powers.
An electric circuit is a source for electricity (battery) and a load (light bulb). This circuit is connected in a "circle" of wires.

The battery gives the force (voltage) that makes the electrons move. The electrons move through the wires of the circuit. When the electrons get to the light bulb they give it the power to make it work. But it only works if the electrons can move forward to the battery again to complete the circle.
Let’s find out more about electric circuits! I will help you.

An electric circuit is a circle through which the electrons flow. You can make a circuit by linking electrical components together with pieces of wire cable. Let's try that now!

I set up my own electric circuit, but one piece is missing. What I do need now are materials that are 'conductors'. They can conduct the electricity to complete my electric circuit.
Not all materials are conductors. Some of them are 'insulators'. They can not conduct electricity so they will not fix my electric circuit.
